{{Short description|On solutions of 7th-degree equations}}
{{No footnotes|date=January 2021}}
'''Hilbert's thirteenth  problem''' is one of the 23 [[Hilbert problems]] set out in a celebrated list compiled in 1900 by [[David Hilbert]].  It entails proving whether a solution exists for all [[Septic equation|7th-degree equations]] using [[algebraic function|algebraic]] (variant: [[continuous function|continuous]]) [[Function (mathematics)|functions]] of two [[argument of a function|arguments]]. It was first presented in the context of [[nomograph]]y, and in particular "nomographic construction" — a process whereby a function of several variables is constructed using functions of two variables. The variant for continuous functions was resolved affirmatively in 1957 by [[Vladimir Arnold]] when he proved the [[Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem]], but the variant for algebraic functions remains unresolved. 

==Introduction==
Using the methods pioneered by [[Ehrenfried Walther von Tschirnhaus]] (1683), [[Erland Samuel Bring]] (1786), and [[George Jerrard]] (1834),<ref>{{Cite book |last=Boyer |first=Carl B. |url=https://books.google.com/books/about/A_History_of_Mathematics.html?id=bR9HAAAAQBAJ |title=A History of Mathematics |last2=Merzbach |first2=Uta C. |date=2011-01-25 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-470-63056-3 |pages=398-399 |language=en}}</ref> [[William Rowan Hamilton]] showed in 1836 that every [[Septic equation|seventh-degree]] equation can be reduced via radicals to the form <math>x^7 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + 1 = 0</math>.<ref>{{cite conference | last = Hamilton | first = W. R.  | title = Inquiry into the Validity of a Method recently proposed by George B. Jerrard, Esq. for Transforming and Resolving Equations of Elevated Degrees | conference = Sixth Meeting of the British Association for the Advancement of Science | location = Bristol | date = August 1836 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Inquiry into the Validity of A Method recently proposed by George B. Jerrard, Esq. |url=https://www.maths.tcd.ie/pub/HistMath/People/Hamilton/Jerrard/ |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=www.maths.tcd.ie}}</ref> 

Regarding this equation, Hilbert asked whether its solution, ''x'', considered as a function of the three variables ''a'', ''b'' and ''c'', can be expressed as the [[function composition|composition]] of a finite number of two-variable functions.

==History==
Hilbert originally posed his problem for [[algebraic function]]s<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hilbert |first=D. |date=1927-12-01 |title=Über die Gleichung neunten Grades |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01447867 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=de |volume=97 |issue=1 |page=246 |doi=10.1007/BF01447867 |issn=1432-1807|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
("...Existenz von algebraischen Funktionen...", i.e., "...existence of algebraic functions..."; also see Abhyankar 1997,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hilbert's Thirteenth Problem {{!}} Société Mathématique de France |url=https://smf.emath.fr/publications/hilberts-thirteenth-problem |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=smf.emath.fr}}</ref> 
Vitushkin 2004<ref>{{cite journal|first=Anatoli Georgievich|last= Vitushkin|author-link=Anatoli Vitushkin|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/links/dd8ef2eead217b7f2f2b8c3b8e0b0b5b/rm698.pdf|title= 13-я проблема Гильберта и смежные вопросы|journal=[[Russian Mathematical Surveys|Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk]]|volume=59|issue=1|year=2004| pages=11–24|doi=10.4213/rm698}} English translation in: {{cite journal| url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/RM2004v059n01ABEH000698|title=On Hilbert's thirteenth problem and related questions |journal=[[Russian Mathematical Surveys]]|volume=59 |year=2004|issue= 1|pages=11–25|doi= 10.1070/RM2004v059n01ABEH000698|mr=2068840 |last1=Vitushkin |first1=A. G. |bibcode=2004RuMaS..59...11V |url-access=subscription}}</ref>).
However, later in that article, Hilbert also conjectured there isn't a solution to a seventh-degree equation, even using arbitrary [[continuous function|continuous functions]] in two variables.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hilbert |first=D. |date=1927-12-01 |title=Über die Gleichung neunten Grades |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01447867 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=de |volume=97 |issue=1 |page=248 |doi=10.1007/BF01447867 |issn=1432-1807|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

A generalization of the second ("continuous") variant of the problem is the following question: can every continuous function of three variables be expressed as a [[function composition|composition]] of finitely many continuous functions of two variables?
The affirmative answer to this general question was given in 1957 by [[Vladimir Arnold]], then only nineteen years old and a student of [[Andrey Kolmogorov]].
Kolmogorov had shown in the previous year that any function of several variables can be constructed with a finite number of three-variable functions.<ref>{{cite|last=A. N. Kolmogorov|year=1956|title=On the representation of continuous functions of several variables by superpositions of continuous functions of fewer variables|journal=Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR|volume=108|issue=2|pages=179–182}}</ref>
Arnold then expanded on this work to show that only two-variable functions were in fact required, thus answering Hilbert's question when posed for the class of continuous functions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=V. I. Arnol'd, “On functions of three variables”, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR, 114:4 (1957), 679–681 |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=dan&paperid=22002&option_lang=eng |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=www.mathnet.ru}}</ref>
Later, Kolmogorov slightly simplified Arnold's result.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A. N. Kolmogorov, “On the representation of continuous functions of many variables by superposition of continuous functions of one variable and addition”, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR, 114:5 (1957), 953–956 |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=dan&paperid=22050&option_lang=eng |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=www.mathnet.ru}}</ref>

Arnold later returned to the algebraic version of the problem, jointly with [[Goro Shimura]] (Arnold and Shimura 1976).<ref>{{cite conference |last1=Arnold |first1=V. I. |last2=Shimura |first2=Goro |title=Superposition of algebraic functions |year=1976 |book-title=Mathematical Developments Arising From Hilbert Problems, Volume 1 |series=Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics |volume=28 |pages=45‑46}}</ref>
